# Durability

## LMDB

Each actor maintains a private **LMDB** environment — a memory-mapped B-tree — with three named databases:

```{=html}
<div class="env-table">
  <div class="env-row"><div class="env-key">inbox/</div><div class="env-val">Raw frame written before fork. Cleared after publish. On restart, unprocessed tuples are redelivered.</div></div>
  <div class="env-row"><div class="env-key">outbox/</div><div class="env-val">Result frame written before publish. Cleared after publish. On restart, unsent results are republished.</div></div>
  <div class="env-row"><div class="env-key">state/</div><div class="env-val">Handler-managed state. Keyed by correlation ID for multi-turn conversations across separate invocations.</div></div>
</div>
```

A crash between fork and publish leaves the tuple in `inbox/`. A crash between result write and publish leaves it in `outbox/`. Either way, the actor recovers on restart with no central coordinator.

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
  participant R as Runtime
  participant H1 as Handler (round 1)
  participant L as LMDB
  participant H2 as Handler (round 2)

  R  ->> L  : inbox.put(tuple_id, frame)
  R  ->> H1 : stdin payload · CORRELATION_ID=abc
  H1 ->> L  : state.put("abc", history)
  H1 ->> R  : stdout result
  R  ->> L  : outbox.put(result_id, frame)
  R  ->> R  : publish to bus
  R  ->> L  : inbox.del + outbox.del

  Note over R: new tuple, same correlation ID

  R  ->> H2 : stdin payload · CORRELATION_ID=abc
  H2 ->> L  : state.get("abc") → history
  H2 ->> R  : stdout final result
```

LMDB provides atomic commits — a crash mid-write leaves the previous state intact.

## Heartbeat

Every actor emits a heartbeat tuple on a timer:

```json
{"id": "worker-1", "inbox": 0, "outbox": 0}
```

Topic: `heartbeat` — TTL: 3× heartbeat interval — Default interval: 5 s

Any actor subscribing to `heartbeat` observes the full mesh state without instrumentation. A debug actor subscribing to `*` sees every tuple on the bus.

## Retry Policy

On handler non-zero exit the runtime retries with exponential backoff:

```{=html}
<div class="env-table">
  <div class="env-row"><div class="env-key">attempt 1</div><div class="env-val">retry after 100 ms</div></div>
  <div class="env-row"><div class="env-key">attempt 2</div><div class="env-val">retry after 200 ms</div></div>
  <div class="env-row"><div class="env-key">attempt 3</div><div class="env-val">retry after 400 ms</div></div>
  <div class="env-row"><div class="env-key">max retries exceeded</div><div class="env-val">drop tuple, log error</div></div>
</div>
```

`ACTOR_RETRY_MAX` controls the ceiling (default 3). A payload exceeding `ACTOR_MAX_PAYLOAD` is dropped immediately — no retry, no malloc.
